tagline: Two old iron towns, and a county seat they fought over.
intro: US 2 runs east out of Iron River through forest past several small lakes to Crystal Falls, where it climbs to meet M-69 beside the courthouse at the top of the hill. The trail ties together the two towns and the mining and logging country between them.

The courthouse was a fight. When Iron County was formed in 1885 the seat went to Iron River, and at one point men from Crystal Falls carried the county records off from the temporary courthouse there. A vote in 1888 went to Crystal Falls by five votes. The next year's vote settled it by nearly a hundred.

moments.title: Stambaugh
moments.text: Platted in 1882 on the site of the Iron River Mine and named for the man who had just bought the mine, the town was folded into Iron River in 2000.

moments.title: Larson Park
moments.text: Herbert Larson set this one out beside the road near Iron River in 1919 and 1920, and it is thought to be the first roadside park in the country.

moments.title: Iron County Courthouse, Crystal Falls
moments.text: Red-brown brick on a hilltop above the business street, with 17-foot zinc statues of Law, Mercy and Justice over the door since 1910.
